result.title: VideoACE: Benchmarking Agentic Video Understanding through High-Frame-Rate Actions
result.summary: Agentic video understanding requires models to actively interact with video environments to gather evidence and form judgments. Evaluating this capability therefore requires assessing whether models can translate opportunities for interaction into better understanding. We introduce VideoACE, a benchmark for assessing video understanding under conditions that support sustained interaction. We focus on high-frame-rate action videos, where rapid, subtle changes make targeted observation especially valuable. The benchmark comprises 1,000 multiple-choice questions spanning six categories of fine-grained action understanding, accompanied by temporal evidence annotations and user hints screened for answer leakage. Its evaluation environment combines video inspection tools with a user simulator, allowing models to adjust temporal coverage, sampling density, and spatial detail, and to revisit evidence and revise their judgments under simulated user feedback. We evaluate single-pass observation, autonomous tool use, and tool use combined with user feedback to examine how effectively models exploit these opportunities. Evaluation of five models reveals distinct patterns in how they acquire evidence and respond to opportunities for further interaction. These findings establish VideoACE as a testbed for examining agentic video understanding beyond performance under a fixed observation setting.

AI.brief_summary: 该论文提出 VideoACE 基准，面向高帧率动作视频，包含 1,000 道细粒度动作理解选择题、时间证据标注与防泄漏用户提示，并提供可调节时间覆盖、采样密度与空间细节、可回溯证据并在用户反馈下修正判断的评估环境。
AI.relevance_reason: 与 LVR 的 THINK/LOOK/STOP 研究直接相关：其单次观察、自主工具调用与结合用户反馈三种设置可供核查视觉证据获取、回溯与停止决策的收益成本，以及多轮观察中证据筛选是否真正影响判断。
